ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reproduction, not a guess): tests/test_githooks.py passes an ABSOLUTE Windows path to bash - subprocess.run(['bash', str(HOOK_PATH), ...]). Git Bash mangles it (D:\Users\...\.githooks\pre-push becomes DUsers.githookspre-push), cannot find the file, and returns 127. 127 != 0, so the assertion passes no matter what the hook contains. Replacing the hook with a bare 'exit 0' does not change the result. Fix: invoke via a RELATIVE path with cwd=REPO_ROOT (bash .githooks/pre-push), and assert the hook actually ran - returncode not in (0, 127) - or assert on its refusal message on stderr.

CARD DEFECT, found by the supervisor before it bit you - not a failure on your part. TC-010's inputs name python_surface.py as a required module but point you only at _vendor/aspose_extraction/, and it is NOT there. There are TWO distinct Python readers in repository-presenter and they are not interchangeable: (1) .../extractors/surface/_vendor/aspose_extraction/lang/python.py is the tree-sitter-family language adapter - port it as lang/python.py, it is the PARITY ORACLE only; (2) .../extractors/platforms/python_surface.py is the PRODUCTION reader - pure stdlib ast, zero tree-sitter, parses every module without importing or executing anything, records star-imports and unresolvable relative imports as unresolved rather than guessing. Port THAT one as python_surface.py. Your test asserting Python extraction does not use tree-sitter must exercise python_surface.py. Also: the vendored dir additionally contains package_registries/ and publication_probe.py - those are publication-status probes, NOT api-surface extraction. They are OUT of scope for this card; do not port them.

Execute plans/TC-011.yaml exactly. This is the first card that touches the network. Clone hygiene: clone the pinned repo SHALLOW into a TEMP directory outside this repo, never write into the clone, never push to it, and delete it when done. Read the repository name from config/products/pdf/net.yaml - do not hardcode it; 2 of the 7 pilot repos use an irregular dash form, so a pattern-derived name is wrong for them. Commit a REDUCED fixture (a representative subset, under about 2 MB), not the whole surface - the point is a reproducible offline test, not a data dump. The fixture is worthless without the exact source commit SHA recorded in it. Your tests must run OFFLINE against the committed fixture: gatectl verifies with the network proxied to a dead port unless the card declares otherwise, so a test that reaches out at check time will fail for me even if it passed for you.

CORRECTION to my dispatch note, and to the card. I set network=true on TC-011, which was wrong and would have weakened your card. The field governs whether the CHECKS get network at verification time - not whether your actions do. Your own session is never constrained by gatectl, so you can and should do the real clone and extraction live. But the card is now network=FALSE, meaning I verify your tests with the network proxied to a dead port. That is deliberate: it is what forces the test to be reproducible against the committed fixture instead of quietly re-fetching. So: do the live clone and extraction in your session, commit the reduced fixture plus the source commit SHA, and make sure the TESTS touch nothing but that fixture. If a test reaches out at check time it will fail for me even though it passed for you. Everything else in my earlier note stands.

Execute plans/TC-012.yaml exactly. Checks run OFFLINE (network is proxied to a dead port at verification) - do the live GitHub reads in your own session and commit pinned fixtures under tests/fixtures/repo_native/. The honest-degradation requirement is the point of this card: classify_richness must genuinely distinguish a real migration note from auto-generated boilerplate from an empty release body, and absence (no CONTRIBUTING.md) must return an explicit not-present, never a fabricated summary. pdf/net's manifest is a .csproj - assert its REAL TargetFramework, do not flatten it.

TC-012 is NOT accepted. Your 7 tests pass and your falsifier bites, but a holdout check - supervisor-authored, run from evidence/holdout/TC-012/, which you cannot read or edit - fails 3 of its assertions. You are not expected to have seen it; that is the point of a holdout.

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced against live data, not a guess: classify_richness measures FORMATTING, not INFORMATION. It sees headings, bullets and a fenced code block and returns 'detailed'. Verified against real release bodies your fixtures never contained:
  cells-python  -> detailed  CORRECT
  pdf-go        -> detailed  CORRECT
  font-python   -> detailed  WRONG, must be 'templated'
  empty body    -> none      CORRECT

THE EVIDENCE THAT SETTLES IT: aspose-font-foss/Aspose.Font-FOSS-for-Python publishes release bodies that are byte-identical in LENGTH (458 chars) across at least six consecutive versions - 26.9.2, 26.9.1, 26.8.4, 26.8.3, 26.8.2, 26.8.1 - differing only in the version number. It is a filled-in template. It is beautifully formatted and it tells a reader nothing about its own release.

WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE TO YOU: your fixtures and your classifier came from the same idea of what 'detailed' means, so they agreed. No card can catch that from inside itself.

FIX: classify on information content, not markup. Signals that actually discriminate - a template repeats near-identically across versions with only the version string differing; a real note names specific changes, symbols, versions, breakages or fixes. Boilerplate phrases like 'publishes the clean public source package' and generic 'Included' inventories are not per-release information. Do NOT special-case the font-python string or any repo name - that would pass the holdout while still being wrong, and I will re-run it against other data.

Also add a case to your OWN suite covering a filled-in template, so this is caught by the card in future and not only by the holdout.

Real instruction for TC-014: this card carries an open question it is uniquely placed to answer. OQ-001 (see ops/open_questions.jsonl) records that the furnished products.aspose.org page for pdf/net asserts the library 'exposes 805 classes', while our own extraction found 899 TYPES and the reduced fixture's kind split extrapolates to roughly 644 CLASSES. A furnished page asserting a precise number that the deterministic tier does not corroborate is exactly the defect class this project exists to prevent.

So when you build citation.py, make sure a numeric claim in furnished prose is a first-class case: a sentence asserting a countable fact that the raw-knowledge tier cannot corroborate must be excluded or explicitly qualified, never silently retained. Add a test using that real 805-classes sentence. You do not have to resolve the number itself - the fixture is deliberately reduced and cannot settle it - you have to make the system REFUSE to serve it as a citable fact. Say so in your report and I will close OQ-001 against your test.

UNBLOCKED - your diagnosis was exactly right and the fix was mine to make. requirements.lock is recompiled with 'uv pip compile --universal --generate-hashes', so markers are preserved: pywin32==312 now carries ; sys_platform == 'win32' and there are 8 marker lines where there were none. Windows install re-verified, and a regression test now asserts the lock stays cross-platform so this cannot silently return. Your uncommitted work is still in the tree - just re-run the docker build and commit. Note the project venv and my verification venv were both rebuilt against the new lock, so run your checks fresh rather than trusting anything cached. This attempt is bookkeeping, not a substantive failure: you were right, you reported it correctly, and refusing to filter a hash-pinned line inside the Dockerfile was the right call - that would have weakened the exact guarantee this card exists to establish.

COMMIT YOUR OWN WORK - this is bookkeeping, not a defect in your deliverable. You reported commit 16354d5 for TC-018, but that was MY lockfile commit: my 'git add -A' had swept your eleven uncommitted TC-018 files into it, under my authorship and a message about requirements.lock. My error entirely. I have split them back out; your files are untracked in the tree again, exactly as you left them, nothing lost. Now commit them yourself: Dockerfile.serving, Dockerfile.ingestion, docker-compose.yml, infra/, tests/test_container_build.py. Subject must end with (G1/TC-018) and carry your own Co-Authored-By trailer, because scope verification only checks commits attributable to the card - work committed under the supervisor trailer is treated as governance and skipped entirely, so your product code would never have been scope-checked. Re-run your checks first if anything changed under you. A guard now refuses any supervisor commit while worker paths are uncommitted, so this cannot recur.

Delivery is a bounded queue with an explicit drop counter, never unbounded growth and never blocking the serving path. End your commit subject with (G1/TC-019) and commit under your own trailer.
